content:
Since it was St Patrick’s Day a few weeks back – and because I’ve just returned from a weekend of pretending to be a hard-drinking, abuse-spitting koala – this week’s 101 Things compilation is all about drinking. And how it is a terribly, terribly fun thing to do.
34 – Design Your Own Cocktail
The first alcohol I started drinking regularly – and continue to drink regularly to this day – is Southern Comfort. One of my own “To Do Before You Die” is to return to the French Quarter of New Orleans and try to work out where McCauley’s Tavern used to be – where SoCo was supposedly invented. Or you know, just do
the SoCo tour.
I’ve always had a sweet tooth with drinks, so I’ve never had any interest in beer because it tastes like bitter despair (an opinion that didn’t win me any friends working in the military or the mining industry), and wine generally seems like an expensive way to turn perfectly good raisins into something as sour as Germaine Greer’s undercarriage (although I don’t mind a sweet “late-harvest” desert wine). So it’s only natural I’d design a cocktail based on Southern Comfort. Although in all honesty calling it a “cocktail” might be a little bit of a stretch… and saying I invented it might be a mild fabrication too…
Liquid Panty Remover (L.P.R)
Take a standard pint glass, and fill a quarter of it with Southern Comfort. Fill the rest with orange juice, and add two teaspoons of sugar. Stir, add umbrella, and lose your mind. Extensive experimentation has shown this is the most dangerous mix for the alcohol sensitive and sugar-addicted (eg. me). An alternative is to remove the sugar and replace half of the orange juice with lemonade – with the lemonade’s fizz hopefully slowing the rate you drink this fractionally.
Oh and ladies before you get offended – it was my panties that used to come off. Back in the dark old days at uni when I wore underwear at all…
65 – Shout “Drinks Are On Me” in a Pub or a Bar
Because I was but a poor student at uni, and because I enjoyed going to bars with army/mining workmates about as much as I enjoyed having poor-man’s A.I.D’s, shouting out “Drinks on are on me” at a bar took until the end of my short “career” in the mining/blasting industry – right around the time the Mighty Ginge started coincidentally.
In fact it was April 20th, 2009 – the last night I was on a mine site.
And hopefully it will forever remain that way…
Since it was my last night at Wodgina (and soon to be decided last night working in the mining industry), the blast crew I worked on convinced me to come down to the site bar for a big night before flying out the next morning. I’d been avoiding the bar like the plague – the last thing I wanted to do was start drinking with the guys I worked with, doing a job I hated 12 hours a day. But I relented, rang the bell (to signal I was paying for everyone’s drinks) and personally got plastered. I still managed to get back to my room afterwards, but not without trying to unlock three other people’s rooms and rip down someone else’s clothes line in the process…
All in all the damage wasn’t that bad – the total came to $100 between a dozen of us. But having a drunken “Deep & Meaningful” conversation with one of my fellow blast crew trying to explain that I didn’t hate him proved to be considerably more expensive emotionally…
93 – Complete the Monopoly Board Pub Crawl
More than any other item on the “101 Things To Do Before You Die” list, writing up the entry for the monopoly board pub crawl has scared me most. Because to do it justice, I feared I’d have to lay out exactly how to do the Monopoly Board Pub Crawl. And having done it twice, the thought of writing the route & schedule all out again was daunting to say the least. Turns out someone has done all the hard work for me.
Let me explain…
For those that don’t know, the Monopoly Board Pub Crawl involves having a drink at each of the 26 properties on the London Monopoly board. You start in Old Kent Road at about 11:45am, and finish in Mayfair around midnight. You traverse all of central London, and it’s actually a great way to see a lot of London if you’re new to it (while getting hammered). But organising one is an outright nightmare – pubs open, close and move all the time. And doing the Monopoly Board Pub Crawl needs to be done on such a schedule you can’t afford to turn up to find a pub not where it needs to be.
In June 2009, I’d just been accepted into the Royal Marines but had to wait until November to start training – so needless to say I was in peak fitness and had plenty of time I do things like research the Monopoly board pub crawl. I found some guys who’d posted how they’d done it in 2001
which helped with about half the properties, but it took a solid week of research to find pubs/bars for each property and what tubes needed to use to get there -
buses were obviously out of the question. Thankfully for people doing it now there’s a dedicated website that’s updated regularly as things change, but in 2009 this was not the case.
There’s no point even trying to describe the crawl itself – as I said, I’ve run two of them now (one in June 2009 with an old uni friend and one of her other mates; the other at Christmas the same year with two of my mates from the marines and the manliest woman I know) – and there’s so much drunken stupidity going on that sharing it all here would spoilt it. I do recommend introducing several rules to spice things up and help you survive though;
Redbull and Vodka at the first stop (Old Kent Road), and the first person to finish their drink at each pub gets to pick what the group drinks at the next stop. This is particularly hilarious when you get a spirit drinker consistently winning (like me), who then gets to watch his beer-drinking buddies fall apart with round after round of shots. - Nothing more than half pints. It’s not being weak – you’re on a 26 stop, 12 hour pub crawl so pace yourself. Try to stick to spirits and liqueurs, otherwise you’ll be fighting for the toilet at every stop. - Which reminds me – print out and laminate a copy of the schedule, then tie it to someone’s wrist. THEN STICK TO THE BLOODY SCHEDULE! The new in-order route gives you a little more time by starting at 10:30am than the one we did (which couldn’t start till 11:45), but once you’ve lost time it’s still a nightmare to make it back. If you lose the route/schedule because of drunken stupidity, your night’s over. - Get something to eat half way through – around Leicester Square is perfect. Again it’s not weak, you’ll pass out somewhere near Bond street if you don’t. And I will not give you a piggyback ride around half the monopoly board … unless you’re hot… - Do NOT make fun of the Custodian helmet the Metro police wear – they may not have guns, but they do have batons. - Everyone wears stupid hats. Removal/loss of hats will result in expensive/unpleasant pub crawl punishments - Have fun
Yes – that’s me in the elf hat, & one of my marine mates in a kimono on top of a lion in Trafalgar Square
Paul Pub Crawl… yes good sir we be doing another one next year! - The Mighty Ginge

Last Thursday was the closest conjunction between Venus and Jupiter in 24 years, so this week’s “101 things” are all about astronomy and the wonders of the night sky.
Now people have been looking up to the heavens for millennia to answer life’s biggest question – if I show her Cassiopeia, will she show me her boobs? And as humanity’s continued existence undoubtedly proves, the ladies love a man that knows how to read the stars. But before I give you all the cheat-sheet on impressing women with your astronomy knowledge, we need to start with the basics…
49 – See both solar and lunar eclipses
An eclipse always sparks off a resurgence of public interest in astronomy, yet a lot people don’t really understand what’s going on. And frankly unless you’re willing to sit down with me, a basketball, a tennis ball and a flash light, and you’re going to put out; I really can’t be bothered explaining it here. Read the wikipedia article. What I can tell you is while most people have probably seen a lunar eclipse, you have to be pretty lucky to see a solar eclipse while you’re
flying over Antarctica. My folks bought me a ticket on the flight over Antarctica to see the November 23rd solar eclipse in 2003. And while having some guy leaning over me for over 20 hours to stare out the window, with a beer gut bigger than I am, wasn’t pleasant it was still worth it.
Shot from the plane window
More recently, I watched last year’s lunar eclipse on December 10th via the SLOOH Space Camera. So if it’s cloudy where you are – or even the middle of the day like this was – you don’t have to miss out on the astronomical goings-on. Highly recommended.
77 – Learn Astronomy and Read The Night Sky
Ladies, hold onto your panties. Gentlemen, pay attention to all the “fun facts” I throw in – repeating them will make it sound like you might know what you’re talking about (when you clearly don’t).
The first thing you need to do is establish where North, South, East and West are.
If you’re in the Northern hemisphere: easy – just find the the “North Star”. The North star is also known as Polaris – Latin for “Pole Star”. It’s actually two stars, and together they are the brightest point in Ursa Minor (aka the “Little Dipper”) - If you’re in the Southern hemisphere: find the Southern Cross (aka “ Crux “). If there’s no bogans around with this tattooed on their back, use the picture below for an idea of what it looks like. Then draw a line along the length of the Crux, and another line that runs perpendicular to the two “Pointer stars”, and where they intersect is South… or just use the picture below. If this proves too difficult, you can a) just use a compass, or b) simply plan to romantically watch the sun set with your lady friend, and take note that where the Sun sets is West, and you can working out North, South and East from there. Shneeeeeaky… It also gives you a chance to point out that the first “star” to appear after sunset is actually a planet – Venus. And Venus is named after the Greek Goddess of Loooooove.
It also has temperatures over 400 degrees Celsius, clouds of sulphuric acid, and is the closet thing we know of to the medieval vision of hell – maybe don’t mention that…
Okay, we know where our four compass points are! Using East and West, follow the arc across the sky that the sun followed (or that the moon is following). This is the ecliptic path, and is also the path all the planets follow. Venus is going to disappear below the horizon within a few hour after sunset, but Mars, Saturn and Jupiter are usually pretty easy to spot – they’ll be bright stars on or near the ecliptic line. And as I mentioned at the start, Venus and Jupiter are within two finger widths of each other at the moment. They won’t all be visible all the time, but if there’s a bright star along the ecliptic it’s probably one of the three. You can even usually guess the planet too – Mars is red, Saturn is a brilliant yellow/white, and Jupiter is larger and it’s colour somewhere in between Mars and Saturn.
Now if you’re not getting laid at this point, I doubt any amount of amateur astronomy is going to cut it. You’re only saving grace now is to a) try and learn the constellations, or b) break out your smart phone and boot up Google Skymap. Try and avoid being one of those clowns who say “I’ll just use my phone” to every one of life’s problems when you do though. But pointing your phone to the sky with Skymap will show you everything – planets, constellations, meteor showers, comets, satellites, everything. It’s also a great bullshit tester for others trying to get in on your astronomy-based heart-throb act.
Just make sure you turn the night vision mode ON – what’s the point of looking at the stars through your phone if you can’t see the actual stars when you look away from the screen?
“What stars?”
And who knows – you may develop a genuine interest in astronomy out of it! Don’t expect to continue getting laid if you do though, unless of course you appear on national television in a possum suit …

content:
If you’ve been diving with sharks since you were 12, you know filling in #2 of the 101 List (Swim With…) is always going to be a laugh.
Swim with… Sharks
Bronze Whaler - photographed near Gnaraloo Station April 2009 Diving regularly in Australia inevitably means being in the water with sharks of one type or another. But ultimately sharks get a really bad rap – at the end of the day they’re just another fish, and most of them terrified of humans. The only time I’ve ever felt threatened by sharks is when we’ve been spear-fishing (and having a fish bleed into the water) in areas where larger sharks are known to be common – it’s a calculated risk based on experience and healthy respect for animals that are only acting under instinct in their natural environment. But here’s a few of my more notable experiences with sharks. 8 foot Wobbegong Shark – Off the coast of Perth, October 1997 I’d completed my PADI Junior Open Water Course a few days after my 12th birthday, and my Dad (who’d been my instructor) had taken me out for several dives in the months since. On a few of these post-course dives we’d come across Port Jackson Sharks which were receptive to being held and patted. It might seem surreal to be 12 and holding a shark across your lap, patting it like a dog, but these “sharks” are quite harmless and are regularly found in aquarium touch pools.
And ADORABLE! Port Jackson’s do however have tails that could (if you’re 12) be confused with that of the much larger and far more aggressive Wobbegong – a carpet shark that (like Port Jackson’s) sit on the bottom of caves and will leave a nasty bite. Also, they have teeth that hook backwards preventing them from letting go once they’ve bitten down. So not to be disturbed – for example – by a 12 year old scuba diver that’s seen just it’s tail sticking out of a cave, and tried to pull it out thinking it’s a Port Jackson. The wobby had swum into a cave then stuck his tail out through a hole in the reef. I’ve spotted the tail, thought it was a Port Jackson and tried to pull him out to say hello. And when he didn’t come out, I started pulling harder and harder… Dad turned around to see why I’d fallen behind, only to get the full view – seeing me standing on top of the reef pulling a shark’s tail, and being able to see the massive Wobbegong going mental underneath as I tried to drag a 4 foot wide animal out through a 1 foot hole. Dad started waving frantically to tell me to let go, so I did. The wobby took off like a rocket out from under the reef, straight toward Dad, only to swim right by him and off into the abyss. Needless to say, these days I like to check exactly what I’m dealing with before I go grabbing animal tails underwater. 15 foot Tiger Shark – Gnaraloo Fishing Station, April 2001 Gnaraloo has been an annual pilgrimage for my Dad and his diving/fishing mates since time began – every April they drive 12 hours to get there, sleep in a sheep shed for two weeks fishing and free-diving every day. By my first trip in 2001 I’d already had a bit of experience dealing with sharks while spear-fishing, and within a few days of being in Gnaraloo we’d been chased out of the water by an aggressive hammerhead that started circling and tried to eat the bag full of speared fish. But toward the end of the trip we had about an 8 foot Bronze Whaler (same species and similar size to the shark pictured at the top) swim into where we were spearing. You can usually tell when a shark is around because all the fish start to become scarce. There’s usually a few fish still swimming about though – but this time there eerily everything disappeared. And sure enough, Dad and I saw the Bronze Whaler and started to head back to the boat to move – there’s no point trying to spear fish if a shark is scaring them all away. And that’s when a 15 foot tiger shark loomed out of the darkness and bit the bronze whaler in half.
When the sharks start eating other sharks - YOU NEED TO GET OUT OF THE WATER I’d just like to point out that an 8 foot Bronze Whaler is a formidable shark in itself – while they’re not known to attack humans unprovoked, they do harass spear-fishers – as I’d discovered a month after the wobbegong, when Dad and I had finished a dive (in a place called “Shark Bay” strangely enough) with me latched onto Dad’s back as he was pushing away a circling 6 foot black tip shark with a speargun, while a 10 foot bronze-whaler shark swam around directly underneath us. So watching a tiger shark eat a Bronze-Whaler is enough to a) get you back in the boat in record time, and b) make you wonder if staying in the boat and fishing with a line for the rest of the trip might be a wise move. **Swim with…Whales 90 foot Blue Whale with calf – Ningaloo Reef, May 2008 I’d just started to get back into diving after a few years staying dry, and was about to complete my Divemaster’s qualification when I went on a trip to Exmouth to dive the Ningaloo Reef. We spent a day free-diving with whale sharks, the biggest fish in the world (and not whales). Having an enormous whale shark swim up from the depths straight toward you isn’t an experience you forget easily, and spending a full day swimming with them was amazing. We were incredibly lucky to do that alone. But it wasn’t until the end of the day, when all the boats were heading back to Exmouth, that the whale shark spotter aircraft that was radioing in the locations of the whale sharks spotted the day’s real treat – a blue whale and it’s calf. They were literally going the same way we were on our way back to Exmouth, so the 4 boat contingent maintained a safe distance and took turns individually moving in closer for a slightly better look. We kept our distance, but to say it was huge is an understatement – even the calf was longer than our boat. And while technically we didn’t swim with the blue whale and it’s calf, I wouldn’t have wanted to. I was lucky enough to see a humpback and a calf a few years later, during a tech dive on my Extended Range course, that decided to briefly swim by in the distance during a decompression stop. But nothing could compare to spending 15 minutes in a boat next to the largest species of animal ever known to have existed, purely by coincidence of timing. **Swim with…Dolphins Red Sea Dolphins – Eilat, August 17th 1995 In October 1994, Jordan and Israel signed a peace treaty and began opening their borders. My family was living in Aqaba – on the Jordanian side of the Red Sea – when it happened because Dad was working for King Hussein at the time. Being 9 and watching Israeli army engineers clearing land mines live on CNN, and knowing the engineers were the same black dots we could see in the distance from our balcony was a fairly surreal experience. But the opening of the border meant we could visit Eilat – the Israeli city directly opposite Aqaba. It was still pretty difficult to get permission to cross the border into Israel for the day (and Dad couldn’t come with us), so Mum only took my sister and I a couple of times. But the most memorable trip across the border was August 17th 1995, on my 10th birthday, when we visited Dolphin Reef to swim with the dolphins. I’d paddled with dolphins at Monkey Mia when I was younger, but this was the first experience I’d ever had swimming with them. We spent most of the day there – I was in and out of the water with the dolphins, eating ice cream and drinking Coca Cola (Coke and Pepsi had drawn up battle lines too – you couldn’t buy Coke in Jordan, Pepsi couldn’t be found in Israel) and making the most of a completely surreal birthday.
Swim with… Tropical Fish**
Growing up on the Red Sea meant there was never any shortage of tropical fish to snorkel with (I was too young to dive). And diving the Ammunition Jetty in Ningaloo is one of the most overwhelming experiences you’ll ever had – there is so much life down there. I started to get fairly serious about underwater photography in the 6 months before I completed my diving instructor training, so rather than talk all the tropical fish I’ve seen, I’d much rather show you some of my favourites – here’s the underwater photo album from my last Gnaraloo trip in 2009. Enjoy. - Share this: - Digg
title: Website – 101 Things (2 Swim With…)

Task
Host a perfect Australia Day BBQ without having it spoilt by bogans.
Background
January 26th – Australia day. The day Australians collectively decide for one day of the year to mildly give a shit about anything. It’s a day we all bask in a little national pride, acknowledge some of our truly inspirational country-people, and inevitably have a BBQ. But an ever-present threat looms over every Australia Day festivity: the bogan.
This is how the world ends – not with a whimper, but with a flannel shirt
For non-Australian readers not familiar with “bogans”, they’re a sub-species of Australian that evolved from exposure to a virus that lives in the fumes produced specifically by 8 cylinder engines (known by bogan-kind as a “Vee-Aite”). Similar yet unrelated sub-species can be found in the Scotland (“Neds”), Canada (“Hosers”) the U.S. (“Rednecks”) and the U.K. (so-called “Chavs” or “B.N.P members”).
Since their initial split from the rest of humanity, bogans have developed their own culture and society – operating within the larger Australian community, but at the same time deliberately offensive to those they consider “un-Australian”. And while their herds are carefully maintained by adding chemical sterilisation agents to Victoria Bitter beer and Winfield Blue cigarettes (bogan translation: “Vee-Bee” & “Win-knee blooz”) the peak of their year-round mating season coincides with Australia Day – resulting in Australian cities being over-run by dickheads with Southern cross tattoos and wearing Australian flags as capes, that have bent a coat-hanger roughly into the shape of Australia and stuck it where their perfectly functional car’s radio antenna was.
“We’re here to make sure neither you or your tattoo reproduce, Jaydenn”
Due to their artificially boosted numbers and the bogan’s instinctual ability to sniff out a flame-grilled sausage from 2000 meters – bogan invasion is the primary threat to any Australia Day BBQ. To counter this, I’ve put together a guide to hosting the traditional Australia Day celebrations without it being spoilt by some mullet-wearing douche-bag ranting in your ear for 6 hours about “national pride” and how Pauline Hanson is a role-model for all Australian women.
To Host or Not to Host, That is the Question
Do you host your own Australia Day BBQ? If you’re not hosting, you need to ask one very important question – do you trust the actual host to screen bogans from the invite list? If you do, relax – you can just rock up with some drinks and meat to throw on the BBQ, and enjoy the day! But bogans can be incredibly sneaky at concealing their identity most of the year, with recent generations learning to infiltrate groups of friends and pass off their behaviour during the year as a “bit of harmless fun” – only to admit their true nature on Australia Day.
If your host invites anyone who;
Has a fresh southern cross tattoo, or has a southern cross tattoo at all
Arrives to the party driving any vehicle with a “Fuck off, We’re Full” sticker on it
Arrives to the party driving an F-Series truck or “fully-sick” ute they bought from working in the mines,
Uses the phrase “fully-sick”
Walks into the party a) with a mullet, b) wearing flannel, or c) carrying a case of “bogan beer” (eg. V.B. or XXXX)
Is known to rock out to AC/DC without a shred of irony
Is known to cry to Cold Chisel’s “Khe Sanh” or Redgum’s “I Was Only Nineteen”, even though both songs were released atleast 10 years before they were born.
then you may be heading to a party that’s destined to be spoilt by bogans. If the host has been known to show any of the behaviors listed above, or you pull up their address on Google Streetview only to see a car on blocks out the front – you’ve been invited to a bogan ambush.
Keep driving – Don’t look back to see if they’re following, just drive as fast as you can
If there’s any doubt about your host’s anti-bogan credentials, it’s probably safer to host it yourself. If however you apply the same criteria to yourself and discover you are a bogan, please disregard – I’d recommend turning up to a friend’s place in your flannel, trying to hit on the host with your best Chopper impersonation, getting blind drunk then driving home in your “fully-sick” V8.
Alternatively, you could stay at home with this song on repeat and re-evaluate some of your life-choices.
Hosting Essentials
So you’ve decided to host a BBQ yourself. Firstly, have you selected the correct location? If you’re considering the South Perth foreshore, I would highly suggest finding another venue – besides being the cultural Medina for all bogan-behaviour (the cultural Mecca ofcourse being Frankston, aka. Frankghanistan), you’re also liable to find yourself in the hot-zone when the fireworks barge catches fire – a spectacle I had the fortunate of witnessing in 2007 from the American Consular General’s residence in King’s Park, watching as the bogans scattered below while I ate prawns and lamb chops.
Which reminds me – serve lamb at your Australia Day BBQ, or Sam Kekovich will turn up and shoot your dog.
Provided you’ve vetted the invite list for potential bogans, picked a venue with a low bogan-hazard level, and served lamb; you’re almost there. Besides obvious things like buying all your booze and ice the week before to avoid the last-minute rush and inevitable price-hikes, your final consideration should be music. This needs to be carefully considered – playing Triple J’s Hottest 100 countdown is a national institution, but any bogan walking by your house it is likely to come bursting through the door. So instead, I’d recommend investing in a heavy-duty cricket bat – there’s a certain cruel justice in chasing a bogan out of your house with a sporting item invented by the English that bogan’s have decided to claim as their own.
Happy Australia Day Everyone
Mighty Ginge Final Note: I’m hosting an Australia Day Special on StroudFM starting at 8pm this Wednesday night (4am Jan 26th for W.A. listeners, 6am Jan 26th for the East Coast), inflicting purely Australian music on the people of Stroud, Gloucestershire.
Listen in live at stroudfm.co.uk or a recording will be available for download in the Media section immediately after broadcast.

content:
As you might have guessed from the tone of the posts since we’ve restarted, this isn’t really the time of year I feel like spreading love and joy (jove? loy?) with the world. We’re coming down off the high of all the family love of Christmas, and the fuzzy memories of our crazy New Year’s antics are starting to fade. So what do we have to look forward to now?
Valentine’s Day…
Now, I get it – it’s a chance for people to celebrate their love for their partner through buying chocolates, flowers, obscene soft toys – not the cool soft toys I collect, but little teddy bears holding red hearts – and a variety of other crap to “show you care”. But for singles like yours truly, I DREAD Valentine’s day. It’s not because most women in the U.K. and Australia treat ginger hair like it’s a symptom of the Ebola virus; nor is it because I’m a bitter, hateful little man that pours scorn on anyone who’s open about love – quite the opposite.
Clearly, I’m here to be all rainbows & lollipops
It’s because it turns out most people regularly lie in relationships to make them “work” anyway, and Valentine’s day is the day these lies and emotional misgivings culminate in some sort of squishy dreamland where couples are convinced they’re in the “perfect relationship”. “Noooo, honey! Ofcourse you don’t look fat in that leopard-print crop top!”, “Curry chips and cider on the beach? You’re such a romantic!”, and my personal favourite: “OFCOURSE I love you Josh!”
Not that we should really be surprised it’s the focal point of so much emotional fabrication. If you trace back the traditions and history of Valentine’s Day, it basically all comes from 1382 when some musty old English poet decided to steal a random saint’s fest day and arbitarily make it a day for lovers just because the king was getting married. So I’ve decided if that guy can steal a Roman festival, and Pippa Middleton’s bum can steal an entire royal wedding, then I’m allowed to steal Februrary 7th and rename it “Ron Burgundy Day” in honour of Ron Burgundy from Anchorman.
Ladies, please refrain from throwing your panties at the screen
Ron Burgundy showed no fear in telling women what he felt about them – as such “Ron Burgundy Day” is about singles telling each other exactly how they feel… in their pants. Personally, I think we just need to be in touch with how we’re really feeling, without the over-the-top gooey bullshit. Sexual testimony, Erotic exposition – whatever you want to call it. And it’s exactly a week before Valentine’s Day, in the hope all this “amourous honesty” will splash over and stop Valentine’s Day being so cheesy and false.
There are a few basic traditions to Ron Burgundy Day – obviously, the traditional greeting of the day is “Just going to put it out there… I want to be on you” – which you can shorten to simply “I want to be on you”. However if someone greets you in this manner on Februrary 7th, tradition dictates there are only three ways you’re permitted to respond;
1st – Scream “TAKE ME TO PLEASURE TOWN!”
Now this may seem a little too eager. But lets be honest – if you’re going to put out, why wait on formalities?
“Look, the most glorious rainbow ever” “Oh! Do me on it!”
2nd – “When in Rome!”
Quite clearly, this phrase makes no sense in the context – which perfectly reflects your initial uncertainty, but wary willingness to see where thing go…
3rd – “I’m sorry, my religion prevents it”
We need to respect people’s religious beliefs. And it might be your religion not to sleep with anyone except your partner. It might also be your religion to not ever sleep with anyone who walks up and says “I want to be on you” – whatever. It’s your religion. But if you DO end up talking and find they’re interesting, you can’t sleep with them till after midnight. I’m sorry, but there are traditions to be respected here. So till midnight, absolutely nothing beyond mutual masturbation.
Also, since this is the only response that automatically precludes sex, it makes Ron Burgundy Day a very exciting time to be an atheist.
“I want to be… ” “Sorry, I think I just found Jesus”
And while Valentine’s Day gladly excludes singles, Ron Burgundy Day has no such discrimination against couples – just be honest with your partner about what you want! Ladies, tell him it’s not a headache – it’s that the thought of him thrusting away for 3 and a half minutes then rolling off and falling asleep makes you feel physically ill. Men, ask your lady to put the toilet seat back up once she’s finished.
The only thing I request… nay, demand: You HAVE to wear a condom. I don’t care if “putting it on will ruin the mood”, or if you’re fatally allergic to latex – if I’m giving you a sex-based holiday tradition, I am NOT taking the blame when 9 months later November 7th rolls around and everyone is popping out little passive-aggressive Scorpio babies.
So in conclusion;
There’s a Facebook event for Ron Burgundy Day – I highly recommend taking part, flirting with each other on the wall, then getting out there and telling people you want to be on them. God knows I will be.
I’ve written a short ukulele serenade in celebration of Ron Burgundy Day. Traditionally a serenade is a song about how beautiful a woman is and how the singer isn’t worthy of her. And it’s not done on a ukulele (aka The Guitar Made for Hobbits). But because it’s written in the spirit of Ron Burgundy Day, this a serenade is more about being open and honest about who I am, and letting the ladies out there decide once they have all the facts. Gentlemen, feel free to copy it onto a tape and play it through a boombox, while standing outside a girl’s window (preferably in the rain). It’s not about you, but if she’s still up for it after hearing this you’re onto a winner. Full and final disclosure – I stole all the chords from a match.com advert.
Ladies, please don’t flood the comments section all at once – The Ron Burgundy Day Serenade

content:
Task
Achieve global infamy and be hunted by every major government on the planet by becoming an international super villain
Background
Super heroes. They’re always out there proclaiming their holier-than-thou bullshit, being an oppressive force for “good” and living in a world of black and white. They fly around making women swoon and men feel physically inferior. Let’s be honest: super heroes are jerks. And the people who like super heroes are shallow, pointless and intellectually-restricted life forms.
But what if you discovered evidence that finally brought Batman out of the closet? What if you had information that showed that Superman’s own home planet was more segregated than South Africa under Apartheid? Would you be brave enough to step up and reveal this for the good of people everywhere? Knowledge is power – would you share with humanity information that showed people their heroes were not who they claimed to be? And would you be ready for the reprisals from both their fans and the superheroes themselves?
Being an effective international super villain takes years of preparation, a single-mindedness to your manifesto, and the intellect to be 5 steps ahead of the modern day paladins who’s reputations you’re tarnishing. But if you are up for a life changing/threatening challenge, I encourage you to read on.
Essential Personal Qualities of An International Super Villain
Be Australian – One of the most under-rated components of any true super villain is being Australian. All of the best movie villains are either Australians playing Americans, Australians playing malfunctioning software, or just Australians straight out playing evil Australians. We’re all know for being easy-going psychopaths, and an effective super villain should endeavour to either become an Australian citizen or at least develop an Australian accent.
Study Physics and Computer Science – Real super villains are almost always socially-inept geeks lashing out at the world. People who relate easily to others aren’t excessively suspicious. Socially-comfortable people don’t throw their entire existence into studying the physical world or complicated operating systems because they find human beings irrational and confusing. Normal people don’t try and satiate their inherent need for basic physical contact by violently pressing their genitals against others in a university common room, while screaming “YOU’VE BEEN RAVAGED!”, nor do they attempt to justify this absurd behaviour through the construction of an elaborate point-based game*.
Develop the super villain “look” and be quirky/mysterious – Hard to describe yet instantly recognisable to all; having the distinct super villain look is an obvious necessity. While nature may not have blessed you a cleft-lip or a parasitic twin, environment can go a long way toward making you look like a super villain. For instance, you could turn your hair a creepy super villain white, by having the federal police raid your house and being convicted of hacking a major overseas telecommunication company the very same year your wife leaves you with your child. Real super villains are also fugitives - running from the omnipotent powers for “good”. They’re always working and developing their plans on the run.
Have a lair - This may seem counter-intuitive given the super-villain’s constantly moving existence, but having an evil lair is important to provide a centralised powerbase. This provides a focus point for all of his data that is both physically and electronically secure – say by putting your servers in a Cold-War era nuclear bunker just outside Stockholm. Of course, a real super villain prepares for the possible destruction of his lair by spreading his resources; caching plans and intelligence all over the globe. And ofcourse, the best villains make the public accomplices in their dastardly acts too…
Turn everyone against each other – The best comic book villains don’t just attack the fabric of society -they turn super heroes against each other as well. You could try making up a lie about your super hero nemesis, and tell another super hero. You lie is easily checked, proven to be just that, and you wind up looking stupid. Instead, it’s always so much better to let the cold hard truth tell the story instead. Just expect your newly embarrassed enemies to come after you with everything they’ve got (and even things they don’t have) while trying to hide the awful truth you’ve exposed…
And there you have it – some of the basic ingredients to becoming an international super villain. Don’t forget, others will quickly follow in your footsteps then try to discredit you. But who knows – if you work hard and strive toward true Machiavellian brilliance, one day you could have the wicked witch of the west screaming for your blood too
* MG: I have it on good authority that this particularly frightening “game” was common for several years in the Applied Physics department at an unnamed university in Western Australia.
title: Website - How to be an International Super Villian

content:
Task
Avoid certain death when faced with the unrelenting horror of the Australian bush
Background
For generations Australians have lived out a happy and BBQ-filled existence next to the ocean; care free in the knowledge that little changes on the fringes of this large and sunburnt country. And given that nearly 3/4 of all Australians live in coastal areas, our laid-back demeanour is probably well deserved. But what about the Australians who don’t live on the coast?
“Bushies” are a breed of their own – welcoming and hospitable at times, they’re also always slightly distant. City folk sometimes struggle with this, thinking them rude. But a true bushy has learnt to keep distance with everyone. Why? You’d probably find it hard to be close to people when you’ve seen relatives, friends and neighbours mercilessly slaughtered by marauding packs of drop bears.
The average bushie has seen the trauma these unrelenting beasts can inflict on communities, and so they are often reluctant to get close to anyone new unless they become another victim. Add in the constant threat of hoop snakes, yowies, and the dangers of using electric trees – violent death is ultimately inevitable for any city folk spending more than a few hours in the Australian bush. However, through knowing the characteristics of some of the more dangerous characters in the Australian bush, it is possible to visit for short periods without becoming an entrée for a Tantanoola tiger.
Drop Bears
An aggressive, carnivorous sub-species of koala – the so-called “Drop Bear” (Phascolarctos Facerapus) is responsible for over 300 fatal attacks each year on humans, with untold numbers of seriously injured survivors. Larger than it’s peaceful Eucalypt-consuming cousins, Drop bears instead rely entirely on a diet of flesh and human breast milk. They only take live prey, dropping from trees onto their target and attacking the exposed neck and spinal cord of their live prey. In the wild these fearsome beasts work in packs to take down much larger animals, and it is here that they present the greatest danger to humans. Other risks however include unsuspecting foreign women being molested by lesbian drop bears, as well as drop bears infiltrating our children’s television shows. However, when not engaged in a hunt or sexual assault, drop bears are highly territorial and regularly fight to protect their carefully constructed hides. Should a drop bear be defeated in a territorial conflict though, it will often summon Beelzebub to assist in destroying the victor.
There are many wide-ranging myths regarding drop bears, and many Australians have used the terror these creatures can create to scare ignorant foreigners even further. Some particularly sick individuals even provide false “security devices” against drop bears. I know of at least one instance where a young, nameless Australian army combat engineer on an exercise managed to convince a company of US marines that drop bears have a weakness for sweet food, and that the only way to save yourself during an attack was to carry around a piece of buttered bread covered in sprinkles in your pocket. The theory was that during an attack, the “Fairy Bread” could be thrown out and the drop bear would stop its violent assault to eat it instead.
Unfortunately when the drop bears did attack the Americans (or more correctly, the marines spotted a harmless koala in a tree one night and blew it away with a salvo of M-16 fire), the fairy bread did nothing. The marines could only start a huge bonfire, fix bayonets, and have all 100 of them stand shoulder to shoulder around the fire, waiting for the inevitable drop bear attack. Unfortunately, this meant the young Aussie engineer that had started this whole lie was booted out of bed by his sergeant, had to drive up to the American camp in the middle of the night and explain that there were no drop bears in the area and that fairy bread did nothing. Not believing him, the Americans stayed encircling the fire till dawn, completely destroying their commanding officer’s plans for the next day.
Totally worth it.
Hoop Snakes
Not as well-known as the terror-instilling drop bear, Hoop snakes (S_cutellatus Lupos)_ still present a significant threat to the overseas visitor. Exceptionally venomous, with no known antivenom, the Hoop snake also opts for the high ground in attacking their prey. However instead of dropping from trees onto their prey like drop bears, hoop snakes will watch from the top of a large, open hill. Upon sighting a potential meal, they will bite their own tail to form a circular “hoop”, proceeding to roll down the hill at their target. Provided they have sufficient velocity, the hoop snake will release it’s tail when it is within 10-15 meters of the target, flying through the air to strike with a fatal bite to the neck.
Fortunately, hoop snake attack can be easily countered if identified during the rolling phase (although once it’s flying through the air at your neck, you’re pretty screwed). By simply running as fast as you can up the hill, the snake will misjudge the release point, flying harmlessly past you and your deliciously tender neck. DO NOT STOP RUNNING THOUGH, as the snake will quickly recalculate it’s tail-release point and still strike. So if you are ever walking past a large, grassy hill and someone screams out “snake!” YOU MUST RUN TO THE TOP OF THE HILL AS FAST AS YOU CAN.
A Final Note of Electric Trees
Some overseas visitors have at times enquired about using the electric trees found in some Australian swamplands to power electric shavers. A common practice for Australian soldiers in the bush is to identify an electric tree (which closely resemble the Paperbark trees found in swamps), push the electric socket into the soft bark of the tree, and proceed to shave off the electric current produced by the tree’s hydro-galvanic reaction.
Overseas visitors are NOT advised to engage in this practice themselves, particularly if using electrical devices designed to handle anything lower than 240 volts. Using an American 120v shaver on a 240volt electric tree has been known to over-volt the shaver, leading to device burn out and cause potentially dangerous facial injuries as the shaver attempts to eat the user’s face
title: Website - Surviving the Australian Bush

content:
Task
Make your own home-made K.F.C at home, with just a few basic ingredients.
Background
Fast Food – it’s the staple of college and university students the world over. But while fast food varies from country to country, there are two trans-fat loaded stalwarts leading the charge globally. And while I’m sure any performing art student (with enough time and grant money) could figure what goes into a big greasy BigMac (and then do an interpretive dance about it), the question continues to hang over Kentucky Fried “Chicken” and it’s ingredients. Nearly 80 years since he first started experimenting with chicken (rather fittingly selling it from a petrol station) during the Great Depression*, the “11 secret herbs and spices” in the Colonel’s “Original recipe” remain unconfirmed.
That was ofcourse, back in the day when “Original recipe” actually had 11 herbs and spices in KFC.
Running a sample in a lab quickly shows that there is SWEET FUCK ALL ingredients in modern KFC. A quick perusal over the web though quickly comes up with a range of different recipes claiming to be the “Original Recipe” (I love you so much Maddox). But since we’ve all been eating a watered down version of the original “Original Recipe” for generations now, I decided instead of trying to copy what you get in the restaurant I’d make a bad-ass version that poor tertiary students can make and consume at their leisure.
Bask in all it’s majesty, and behold for I give you -
The Mighty Ginge’s “Ultra Ball-Breaker Original Recipe”
Ingredients (Serves 1)
1 egg 2 teaspoons of traditional soy sauce 1 cup of Kellogg’s “Crunchy Nut” 1 cup of peanuts 2 teaspoons of honey 1 teaspoon of black pepper 1 freshly shaven kitten (if you’re allergic to cat hair, do it any way – courage wolf will protect you) **
**
Method
Pre-heat your fan-forced oven to 220 deg Celsius (who cares what it is in Fahrenheit? Welcome to the metric system, get with the program) Crack the egg into a large bowl, then add the soy sauce, honey and black pepper – mix thoroughly. Place the cup of Kellogg’s Crunchy Nut and the peanuts** into a ziplock bag, and crush the living monkey Jesus out of it until it’s nearly powder. Added the crushed flakes to the bowl, and again mix thoroughly. Depending on how finely you crushed the flakes, you should be left with a chunky paste of death Take your shaven kitten and dip it into the bowl. Ensure it is covered completely and evenly with the mixture to ensure a consistent bake. This recipe also works by substituting the kitten with either 2 chicken fillets (if you’re a weak little girl) or a fully grown tom-cat that you’ve just dragged out of a pool and is still alive (if you’re the ultimate bad-ass like Blaine Cooper) Bake your kitten on a wire frame with a drip tray for approximately 20mins. The outer coating should just be turning a dark brown when you remove it from the oven. Serve with half a cup of uncooked rice (because that’s how extreme you are) Finally as an additional treat for dessert, scrape the slab of burnt honey that has leached off the mixture and pooled in the drip tray – it’s both delicious and carcinogenic. And for all the Commerce students trying to type “carcinogenic” into Wikipedia, it means “good for you”.
And there you have it – a home made KFC recipe that’s cheap, tasty, and simple enough a humanities student could cook it. You’ll be able to enjoy delicious fried food without having to leave your World of Warcraft character unattended for the 3 minutes it would take to drive to KFC and back.
Enjoy!
* The actual Great Depression, not this “global depression” we’re supposed to be in now. Too bad today’s stock-traders aren’t real men like they were back in the 30′s, where there was literally a hail of Wall Street traders jumping from skyscrapers. What we need is Godzilla to ruin the US Federal Reserve too – that’ll teach you for running a fake economy
**Peanuts play no actual role in this recipe whatsoever, other than to increase the amount of salt in it. But they do serve as a timely reminder to those who are prone to nut-based anaphylactic shock to stay out of my kitchen
title: Website - Home Made KFC

Reference: https://axel-busch.medium.com/how-to-quickly-create-a-3d-model-from-360-underwater-video-in-1h-or-less-b45b1cf29655
Quick Notes Import & split Video **File -> Import -> Video Alignment Tools -> Camera Calibration: Spherical Workflow -> Align Photos (Preselection OFF) Full Details What is the best lighting for underwater 360 video? Recommended 360 degree camera settings for photogrammetry:
Resolution: Highest resolution. Image Quality: Highest quality. White balance: Manual/fixed, not automatic. Exposure: Automatic (generally). max ISO: 200–400 for small sensors, up to 1600 for 1" or larger. RAW Images: Not needed (generally). Sharpening: Off or ‘soft’. Stabilisation: On. Direction lock: On. Rules of thumb for buying a photogrammetry computer:
RAM>CPU>GPU Desktop PC over a Laptop PC How do I create a 3D model from 360 degree video with Metashape? There are five general steps involved in creating a 3D model through photogrammetry:
Import your video/photos — videos will be converted to photos. Align photos — estimate the camera position and orientation at time of capture and match key points across images. Build the point cloud — points in 3D space that represent points on the surface of the model. Build the 3D Model — a triangle mesh model that represents the external surface of the model. Create textures — a texture contains the colour information for every surface area of the model. Step 1: Import video or photos For Video: File -> Import -> Video … Set frame step = 1 photo per second (eg. 24fps = frame step of 24) For Photos: Workflow -> Add Photos… After importing save the project by clicking on the menu item File -> Save. Step 2: Align photos Tell Metashape our images are spherical panoramas.
Click on the menu item Tools -> Camera Calibration Then then the parameter “Camera type” to “Spherical” and press [OK]. Now click on the menu item Workflow -> Align Photos… Set the following parameters in the Align Photos dialog: General:
Accuracy: High Generic preselection: On (OR TURN THIS OFF FOR LONG-SLOW-HIGH ACCURACY ALIGNMENT) Reference preselection: On (OR TURN THIS OFF FOR LONG-SLOW-HIGH ACCURACY ALIGNMENT) Type: Sequential Advanced: Exclude stationary tie points: On Press [OK] Positions of the cameras are displayed as spheres. This can be toggled with: Model -> Show/Hide Items -> Show Cameras
Step 3: Build the point cloud Workflow -> Build Point Cloud… Then set the following parameters in the Build Point Cloud dialog: General:
Source data: Depth maps Quality: High Advanced: Depth filtering: mild Calculate point colors: On Calculate point confidence: On Press [OK] The point cloud can now be edited within the Metashape environment, for example unwanted points can be selected and deleted. The point cloud can also be exported to an external tool for further analysis.
Step 4: Build the 3D model Metashape supports three reconstruction methods:
Tie-points: Very fast, low-detail model based on tie points. Takes seconds. Depth-maps: Slow reconstruction of a high-quality model using the GPU. Point-cloud: Very slow reconstruction of a high-quality model based on the previously reconstructed or imported point cloud. “Depth-maps” is recommended unless the point cloud was edited prior to model reconstruction. To start the reconstruction: Workflow -> Build Model…
Set the following parameters in the Build Model dialog: General:
Source data: Depth maps Surface type: Arbitrary (3D) Quality: High Face count: High (or a desired number e.g. 1,000,000) Advanced: Interpolation: Enabled (default) Depth filtering: Mild Calculate vertex colors: On Reuse depth maps: On Press [OK] To save a new model, leave the parameter “Replace default model” unchecked.
When interpolation is used, Metashape will try to fill holes. This is usually desired and the default setting. These extra surfaces can later always be deleted easily if they are unwanted.
Recommend creating at least two models:
One model with Face count: High, and then Second model with face count below 1,000,000 The second model is more suitable to use for online sharing or in a game engine - Model now shows the shape of our cave very well, but the walls only show very little colour.
Models with a lower face count have less details, but you can use the high-resolution model to create a normal map texture which can recover that detail very well when viewing.
Step 5: Build textures To build textures: Workflow -> Build Texture… Set the following parameters in the Build Texture dialog to build the Diffuse map: General:
Texture type: Diffuse map Source data: Images Mapping mode: Generic Blending mode: Mosaic Texture size/count: 8192 x 1 Advanced: Enable hole filling: On Enable ghosting filter: On Press [OK] Texture type
“diffuse map” is standard colour texture. “normal map” used to add details without using more polygons (faces). Normal maps requires a higher polygon model (>1 million) overlaid on a model with <1 million. Texture size/count Modern devices can easily handle a 8192 texture size. For larger models, one 8192 texture is not enough for adequate detail - generate 4196 x 8, which is the same as 8192 x 2.
Creating the normal map The normal map adds detail to the low-polygon model by extracting “bumpiness” information from a higher-detail model.
Set the following parameters in the Build Texture dialog to build the Normal map:
Texture type: Normal map Source data: 3D model (highest face count) Mapping mode: Keep uv Blending mode: Mosaic Texture size/count: (same as Diffuse map) Press [OK] Export the model The most popular format for 3D files is Wavefront .obj files (OBJ). These files include the textures as external jpg files and a material description file (.mtl) that ties the model and textures together.
What can I do with a 3D model? The most popular use case after exporting a model from the photogrammetry software is probably to share it online. Popular platforms are Sketchfab or Construkted, and I recommend a model size of less than 1M polygons.
Sometimes you might want to edit the model more than what Metashape allows, or just view it on your computer. Popular free 3D viewing/editing softare are Blender and Meshlab. The most popular commercial packages are 3ds Max and Maya.
You can also import the model into a game engine like Unity, Godot, or Unreal and create a walk-through experience or game.
title: 360 Video to 3D Model

Insta - Rage Spikes (Les Grossman) Insta - Showing up after disappearing for months (Exploding Kittens) Insta - ADHD Boyfriend explained by Ducks Insta - Sleeping Position Insta - If you were lazy you’d be having fun Insta - ADHD Needs Autonomy Insta - Autism/ADHD Bingo Insta - ADHD + Autism masking - AuDHD
Outgoing ADHD traits can mask autistic struggles with social rules. How it can show up: Using humour or storytelling to connect (ADHD) Taking things literally and missing hidden meanings (Autism) Struggling with sarcasm or vague hints (Autism) Oversharing or interrupting without realizing (ADHD) Socializing feels like work, not rest (Autism) Being the “life of the party,” then suddenly ghosting without explanation (Overlap) Talking over others out of excitement (ADHD) Flat or monotone tone even when engaged (Autism) Switching topics quickly (ADHD) Using very precise or literal language (Autism) Talking for hours about a passion… but monotone delivery hides how much they care (Overlap) Overcommitting when energized (ADHD) Forgetting personal needs while hyperfocusing on tasks (ADHD) Sudden withdrawal from overload (Autism) Needing long downtime to recover (Autism) Looking unstoppable one week, unreachable the next (Overlap) Burnout cycles repeating across months or years (Overlap) Heightened sensitivity to lights, sounds, or textures (Autism) Repetitive movements like shifting side to side when standing or rotating objects like pens or coins (Autism) Zoning out mid-conversation or task (ADHD) Jumping between tasks when overwhelmed by the environment (ADHD) Using fidgets or restless movement to stay regulated (Overlap) Forgetting everyday tasks (ADHD) Relying on rigid routines to cope (Autism) Starting many projects without finishing (ADHD) Struggling with transitions or unexpected changes (Autism) Planners, apps, sticky notes everywhere… yet still forgetting the one thing that mattered (Overlap) Intense excitement or frustration (ADHD) Crying or anger that feels uncontrollable (ADHD) Shutting down or going quiet under stress (Autism) Emotional reactions triggered by sensory overload (Autism) Feelings that hit fast and linger longer than expected (Overlap) Hyperfocus on special interests (ADHD) Racing through work at the last minute with bursts of energy (ADHD) Deep knowledge in narrow areas (Autism) Needing structure and clear steps to function (Autism) Teachers or bosses see the talent, miss the struggle (Overlap) Peaks of brilliance alongside sudden crashes (Overlap) Making friends quickly (ADHD) Saying yes to plans impulsively, then regretting later (ADHD) Struggling to sustain long-term connections (Autism) Missing subtle social cues (Autism) Friendships feel all-or-nothing, too intense or too distant (Overlap) AuDHD Being seen as “too capable” to need support Burnout cycles mistaken for laziness Sensory or emotional sensitivity dismissed as weakness Inconsistency mistaken for lack of effort AuDHD doesn’t look like one or the other. It looks like both, and neither, all at once. Insta - Exhausted by dumbness, mediocrity
“That’s what’s exhausting about it, because no one is actually saying anything. When you and I have conversations I’m not exhausted by it because we’re talking about things, but when you have these stupid casual, ridiculous, mundane social interactions with the average person every day wherever you’re at, they’re not saying anything that matters. So that’s the part that’s exhausting. There’s probably some kind of energy being spent tolerating boring, mediocre, dumb conversations - that’s more what it feels like. Fighting that off expends energy, so it’s exhausting fighting off dumbness. Dumb mediocrity. Whereas if I’m having an intellectually stimulating conversation and learning things and having differing opinions on important topics, I don’t find that exhausting, I find that energising. I really think that’s part of it - whatever energy is being spent blocking the stupid, which is a lot.” Insta - Trevor Noah on how his depression was actually untreated ADHD
“My depression is created by a severe level of ADHD. It can be different for different people. So for myself it means if I’m not careful in how I sleep, how I eat, how I manage my routine I can become overwhelmed and it can just feel like the whole world is just too heavy to bare.” Insta - Trevor Noah on saying “No”
“Start with no. Changed my whole life. Everything people ask you, start with no, and you’ll be shocked at how it changes. Because that’s what I realised happens to ADHD people. Our brains are moving so quickly, someone says something, we love being stimulated, and so Christiana says ‘Hey, can you babysit my kid this week’ ‘Yeah I’d love to’ I said it immediately. And then I leave the conversation, I pull out my phone, and I go ‘Oh, this weekend I have a gig that I have to do, and I forgot about this thing’ but you send me a text going ‘Thank you so much for agreeing to babysit’ and I go ‘Ahh damn what do I do now? Wait, I think I can do this - what time is the actual babysitting? From 4 to 6, my gig is at 6:30 so I could, it’s a 27min drive - I think I can’. And now I’m back in that loop. And then what happens is I disappoint you on the day because I get overwhelmed. Because the day comes, my times aren’t lining up, I can’t get to you on time and then what happens to a lot of people with ADHD I know is there’s the shame that comes with it. Because you were trying to do the thing for everyone. What happens is you fail everyone. And because, rightfully so on their side, they don’t know what you were going through, and so they just go ‘Why didn’t you tell me, why did you agree to do this?’ Related: Facebook - Hey, could you… “No” Insta - Chaotic Discipline
“You could have something called chaotic discipline. Some days you going to be a big old couch potato. You ain’t going to want to do nothing, you barely want to breathe. You don’t even want to get out of bed to eat, you just want to lay in the bed. But some days your ass is going to be on fire. When you have those on fire days you get a week’s worth of stuff done in a day. When you on fire, you on FIRE! So having ADHD you’re not going to have regular discipline like a normal person. You’re NOT neurotypical, you’re neurodivergent. Your discipline is different from everyone else’s. Neurotypical discipline is more consistent. Your type of discipline is actually more productive. Three days of the week you’re just a couch potato. You don’t want to do nothing, you don’t want to talk to nobody, you’re just laying there. But those other four days of the week you’re getting a month’s worth of work done. So if you got ADHD, don’t feel bad about yourself on those couch potato days. You need those! It’s literally part of your disciplinary action. Because when you get back to those on-fire days, you’re going to be getting everything and anything done.” Related Insta - ADHD - 3 years of therapy in 60sec Superpower - Routine helps, journaling helps This also reminds me of… Insta - Introverts
“Number one - introvert doesn’t mean I actually fucking hate people, it just means I hate the unnecessary actions of fucking people. My energy isn’t fucking low, it’s exclusive. Number two - my quiet isn’t fucking awkward, I’m just deciding if this conversation deserves my extrovert mode or if I should save that energy for something that actually fucking matters Number three - I realised I’m not anti-social, I’m selectively social. I can be the life of the party if it’s the right fucking party. But if it’s small talk and weird fucking vibes I turn into background furniture instantly and then make a fucking excuse to fucking leave Number Four - I learned that I am an introvert by nature but an extrovert by purpose. Put me around my wife, my kids, my fucking mission, my calling, and I’m charismatic as fuck. I’m loud, I’m present, and even fucking more locked in. Put me in a room full of people bragging about absolutely fucking nothing, and I’m going to teleport it - vanish my guy Number Five - Introverts aren’t fucking quiet, we’re intentional. We don’t speak to fill space - we speak to build it. And we don’t show up everywhere - we show up where it fucking counts. And last but not least you don’t need to be on for fucking everyone, just the people in the fucking missions that matter. That’s the real fucking confidence, that’s the real fucking peace. References

About From https://tech-diving.jp/akiyoshidai
What is Akiyoshidai? Akiyoshidai is Japan’s largest karst plateau , located in the central and eastern parts of Mine City, Yamaguchi Prefecture. Its limestone distribution covers approximately 93 km², a scale unparalleled anywhere else in Japan.
More than 400 limestone caves have been identified in Akiyoshidai, including Akiyoshido Cave , one of Japan’s three largest limestone caves and a designated special natural monument.
Akiyoshidai is divided into two plateaus, Higashidai and Nishidai, by the Higashikawa River . Higashidai (Akiyoshidai in the narrow sense) was designated a national park (Akiyoshidai National Park) in 1955 and a special natural monument in 1964. In addition, individual caves are registered as natural monuments, and meticulous care is taken in their maintenance and management.
Akiyoshidai Groundwater System The limestone that makes up Akiyoshidai is thought to have begun forming about 340 million years ago, and then risen to the surface several million years ago. Over long periods of time, this limestone layer was eroded by water, forming a groundwater system, and it is believed that a complex network of underground waterways has now been formed.
The groundwater system of Akiyoshidai has been studied since the 1950s, with a particularly large number of surveys and studies conducted in the 1980s. While some of these included surveys involving actual diving, the limitations of cave diving technology and surveying methods at the time meant that detailed underwater surveys, systematic investigations, and research on the underwater environment were not fully conducted.
Groundwater system of Higashi-Akiyoshidai Underwater surveys of Higashidai, particularly those concerning Akiyoshido Cave, have progressed relatively well. The groundwater system of Higashidai is broadly divided into two parts: the “Kanoide water system” in the north and the “Akiyoshido water system” in the south, with their respective catchment areas estimated at 1,200 hectares and 1,400 hectares. Intermittent surveys have been conducted both on land and underwater at Akiyoshido Cave, and as of December 2017, the total length of the surveys, including both the land and submerged sections, reached 10,700 meters. Approximately 30% of this area is submerged, leaving room for exploring new side tunnels through diving. However,
A certain level of research had already been conducted between the 1970s and 1990s. Akiyoshido Cave is the only cave designated as a Special Natural Monument, and therefore requires more delicate experience and environmental understanding during its investigation. Based on the above points, this project will begin with the Nishidai groundwater system, for which there are relatively few survey examples.
Wildlife Division, Nature Conservation Bureau, Ministry of the Environment, Akiyoshidai Groundwater System, March 2023, 2p. Akiyoshidai Science Museum, “The Cutting Edge of Akiyoshido Cave Research,” 2017, https://karusuto.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/12/event_20171212.pdf Groundwater system of Nishi-Akiyoshidai Compared to Higashidai, Nishidai has fewer underground lakes, and previous research on its groundwater system has been limited.
While there are records of diving in some areas in the past, as far as I could find, there have been no underwater surveys or specific field studies conducted underwater.
The groundwater system of Nishidai is
Atufuku Beppudai Hydrological District Iwanagadai Hydrological District Isadai Hydrological District They can be broadly divided into these three categories.
Within this area, the Ofukubeppu-dai hydrological district contains “Terayama no Ana,” the largest underground lake in Nishidai . In this project, we first considered the possibility of starting a diving survey from “Terayama no Ana.”
It is believed that the groundwater around “Terayama no Ana” drains from west to east, 3) and if this hypothesis is correct, it is possible that “Terayama no Ana” is connected underwater to “Shirakawa no Ike” downstream .
In particular, the groundwater levels at both locations are almost identical at approximately 90 meters, and furthermore, measurements indicate that there is little fluctuation in the groundwater level due to rainfall throughout the year.3 ) Given these conditions, it is possible that they are connected by a relatively large underground waterway , and it can be assumed that there is space through which a person can pass.
Previous studies have stated that “this section was affected by the former intense erosive action of the Koto River, as indicated by the V-shaped valley (Tanaka and Fujii, 1975; Fujii, 1980) buried beneath the downstream Seto Polie, and the cave has expanded considerably downwards. However, due to the rise in groundwater level associated with the deposition of alluvial deposits, this lower section is now submerged and cannot be directly observed.” 3) However, conducting a diving survey may allow for the direct observation of the subsurface structure, which has previously only been inferred indirectly.

About Algeria features a diverse landscape that includes mountain ranges, vast deserts, and karstic plateaus, making it highly relevant from a speleological and geological perspective.
🪨 Limestone Karst in Algeria Yes, Algeria has significant limestone karst formations, especially in the northern and northeastern regions of the country. These include:
Djurdjura Mountains (part of the Tell Atlas): This region has well-developed karst plateaus with numerous caves and sinkholes, formed in Jurassic and Cretaceous limestones. **Constantine and Setif regions**: Known for complex karst systems and underground hydrology. Tassili n’Ajjer (southeastern Algeria - DO NOT TRAVEL): While primarily known for its sandstone formations and prehistoric rock art, some karst-like erosion features occur in isolated carbonate outcrops. 🕳️ Caves in Algeria Algeria has extensive cave systems, many of which are of speleological, ecological, or archaeological interest. Notable caves include:
Anou Boussouil: Located in the Djurdjura Mountains, it is one of the deepest known caves in Africa, with a depth exceeding 800 metres. It features vertical shafts, underground rivers, and significant speleothem development.
Anou Ifflis: Also in Djurdjura, with a depth of over 1,000 metres, this cave is often cited as the deepest in North Africa.
Grotte de Gueldaman (near Tizi Ouzou): A significant archaeological cave site with evidence of Neolithic habitation.
⚠️ Travel and Exploration Notes Many of Algeria’s karst areas are located in mountainous regions that are safe and accessible to travelers, especially in Kabylie and parts of the Tell Atlas.
Some areas (particularly south or interior regions) may pose travel challenges due to remoteness or security concerns. Always check Smartraveller before planning expeditions.
Algeria’s caves are relatively underexplored compared to Europe or Southeast Asia, offering opportunities for new speleological discoveries, though permits and local collaboration may be required.
Summary Yes, Algeria is rich in limestone karst and contains many caves, including some of the deepest in Africa. The Djurdjura Mountains are particularly notable for their karst terrain and vertical caves, making the country an intriguing — though logistically demanding — destination for karst and cave exploration.

Allendale East Cave
Introduction Known as the hole in the middle of the road or just ‘the Dale’, Allendale East Cave is a very popular site among the CDAA Cave rated divers in the Mount Gambier region. As it presents itself as a non-complex cave to dive in, the Soggy Wombats Team has been training, developing skills and accumulating experience in this cave since 2019. Although geographically far from the most developed cave systems in the region, ‘the Dale’ has a small ‘tunnel’ at it’s deepest end that has been in most of Australian’s Cave Divers dreams to break into something big. There hasn’t been any breakthrough in this cave in the last 20 years or so, but with the advances in exploration techniques, we might be surprised with what the future will tell us.
Line Survey and Photogrammetry Although the first line survey produced by the Wombats using the MNemo goes back as early as 2020, Allendale was surveyed only in 2022. The photogrammetry model produced by the Wombats in the same year was the first full cave model we produced and helped shape the equipment settings and configurations we used for future photogrammetry projects.
One of the great features of the MNemo it to give you a quick general idea of the direction the cave is heading. Grubby Wombat was the first Wombat to play with the first version of the equipment back in 2019. Most recently the wombats are using the MNemov2 in their projects. Check more information regarding how to learn and use MNemo in your projects in this article in our page.
Overlay of the Wombats’ first line survey in the Allendale East Cave.
Photogrammetry is a powerful tool, however a little complex to dominate in an dark, underground water filled environment. The Wombats used Allendale as the ‘playground’ to firstly understand and later develop different techniques of data gathering and how the available software deals with them.
Out of the first model produced by the Wombats, they have produce their first digital contour line map through CloudCompare. As divers, producing a map that can give you precise information about depth is fundamental for dive planning.
Later, using the Professional version of Agisoft Metashape and multiple trial and error attempts, the Wombats were able to merge surface and underwater scans. The accuracy of the model scale has been confirmed through measurements of objects inside the cave (drum barrel) as well as depth and overlaying geo-referenced maps (via GoogleMaps).
We prepared a ‘swim through’ video of the Allendale Cave (check above). You can have a good idea of what will be your dive before you get there through it.
If you would like to explore the models, we are hosting them in Contrukted Reality and Sketchfab. They offer different features and it felt like we’d like to share both with the wider community. To check the main features of the cave and understand it’s plan view, check the model in Sketchfab. If you would like to navigate by yourself through the cave, check the Construkted Reality model.
Most of the information and documents we produced are available in CaveDB. We have partnered with them as an intent to maintain all produced information free and accessible to anyone in the cave diving community or the broader public.
As an outcome of all the data we collected, an updated map of the Allendale East Cave overlaying the cave and the surface features has been produced. Let us know if you’d like a high resolution of the map.
title: Allendale East Cave – Soggy Wombats

About Area of Interest: Vayots Dzor, Syunik, Tavush Moderate to High Cave Potential
Large parts of Armenia’s landscape are limestone and dolomite, particularly in the Vayots Dzor, Syunik, and Tavush provinces. Features rugged terrain with karst valleys, dolines, and numerous caves, many of which are still actively being mapped by local and European caving groups. Known Caves Mozrov Cave, Magili Cave, and Arjeri Cave are significant dry caves. Armenia is known for deep fissure systems and vertical caves — some of which contain seasonal sumps or intermittent water pools. Cave Diving Status No published records of cave diving expeditions. Numerous karst springs, resurgences, and hydrothermal systems may offer dive potential, particularly at mid-altitudes where the water table is accessible. Exploration Potential High chance of discovering new phreatic or resurgence caves. Requires satellite scouting and geological mapping to identify high-potential karst spring zones. Local geology and hydrology suggest first-descent opportunities, especially during spring melt (April–June). Caves Mozrov Cave Magili Cave Arjeri Cave Trips References
